answer: Graph factorization is generally applicable when the graph can be represented as a weighted adjacency matrix and the goal is to learn low-dimensional embeddings by approximating that matrix; in practice it is most natural for static, relatively small-to-medium graphs because it relies on matrix factorization over the whole graph. LINE is more broadly applicable to large-scale graphs, including very large sparse networks, because it is designed to optimize first-order and/or second-order proximity with efficient edge-sampling and negative-sampling style training, so it scales much better than standard graph factorization. In short: graph factorization is more limited by graph size and the need for a matrix-form representation, while LINE is applicable to much larger graphs and is specifically built for scalability.
